title: Unlawful assembly
old_text: IPC Section 141 defined unlawful assembly (assembly of 5+ persons with common object to overawe government, resist law, commit mischief/trespass, or enforce right by force); Sections 142-145 penalized membership, armed membership (up to 2 years), and failure to disperse.
new_text: Sub-section (1) defines unlawful assembly of five or more persons with five statutory common objects; Sub-section (2) punishes basic membership with imprisonment up to six months, or fine, or both; Sub-section (3) punishes membership armed with deadly weapons with imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both; Sub-section (4) punishes joining or continuing after command to disperse with imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both.
punishment_old: Basic membership (IPC 143): up to 6 months or fine; Armed (IPC 144): up to 2 years or fine; Continuing after command (IPC 145): up to 2 years or fine.
punishment_new: Basic membership (189(2)): imprisonment up to 6 months, or fine, or both; Armed with deadly weapon (189(3)): imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both; Continuing after command (189(4)): imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both.
explanation: Consolidates five consecutive IPC sections (141 through 145) covering the definition, membership, armed participation, and failure to disperse of an unlawful assembly into a single structured section with four subsections.

title: Every member of unlawful assembly guilty of offence committed in prosecution of common object
old_text: If an offence is committed by any member of an unlawful assembly in prosecution of the common object, or such as members knew likely to be committed, every person who at the time is a member is guilty of that offence.
new_text: If an offence is committed by any member of an unlawful assembly in prosecution of the common object of that assembly, or such as the members of that assembly knew to be likely to be committed in prosecution of that object, every person who, at the time of the committing of that offence, is a member of the same assembly, is guilty of that offence.
punishment_old: Constructive liability: punished with the penalty prescribed for the specific offence committed (IPC Section 149).
punishment_new: Constructive liability: punished with the penalty prescribed for the specific offence committed (BNS Section 190).
explanation: Retains the foundational doctrine of constructive or vicarious liability for members of an unlawful assembly. Renumbered from IPC Section 149 without substantive change.

title: Rioting
old_text: IPC Section 146 defined rioting (force or violence used by an unlawful assembly); Section 147 punished rioting with up to 2 years or fine; Section 148 punished rioting armed with deadly weapon with up to 3 years or fine.
new_text: Sub-section (1) defines rioting (whenever force or violence is used by an unlawful assembly or any member thereof in prosecution of the common object); Sub-section (2) punishes basic rioting with imprisonment up to two years, or fine, or both; Sub-section (3) punishes rioting armed with a deadly weapon or anything likely to cause death with imprisonment up to five years, or fine, or both.
punishment_old: Basic rioting (IPC 147): up to 2 years or fine; Armed rioting (IPC 148): up to 3 years or fine.
punishment_new: Basic rioting (191(2)): imprisonment up to 2 years, or fine, or both; Armed with deadly weapon (191(3)): imprisonment up to 5 years, or fine, or both.
explanation: Consolidates definition (IPC 146), punishment (IPC 147), and armed rioting (IPC 148) into a unified section, while significantly elevating the maximum penalty for armed rioting from 3 to 5 years imprisonment.

title: Wantonly giving provocation with intent to cause riot
old_text: Penalized malignantly or wantonly giving provocation with intent to cause riot with up to 1 year or fine (if riot committed) or up to 6 months or fine (if not committed).
new_text: Whoever malignantly, or wantonly, by doing anything which is illegal, gives provocation to any person intending or knowing it to be likely that such provocation will cause the offence of rioting to be committed, shall be punished with imprisonment up to one year (if rioting committed) or up to six months (if not committed), or fine, or both.
punishment_old: If riot committed: imprisonment up to 1 year, or fine, or both; if not committed: up to 6 months, or fine, or both (IPC Section 153).
punishment_new: If riot committed: imprisonment up to one year, or fine, or both; if not committed: up to six months, or fine, or both (BNS Section 192).
explanation: Penalizes wanton provocations aimed at inciting street riots or public disorder, with graduated sentencing depending on whether rioting materializes. Renumbered from IPC Section 153.

title: Liability of owner, occupier, etc., of land on which an unlawful assembly or riot takes place
old_text: IPC Sections 154, 155, and 156 penalized owners/occupiers of land and their agents who failed to prevent or report unlawful assemblies or riots on their properties, with fines up to ₹1,000.
new_text: Consolidates property owner/occupier liability: Sub-section (1) punishes owners/occupiers of land who fail to give earliest notice to police or suppress unlawful assemblies with fine up to five thousand rupees; Sub-section (2) punishes persons for whose benefit riots are committed; Sub-section (3) punishes agents of owners who fail to take lawful steps to prevent riots.
punishment_old: Dispersed fines up to ₹1,000 across IPC Sections 154, 155, 156.
punishment_new: Fine which may extend to five thousand rupees across subsections (BNS Section 193).
explanation: Consolidates IPC Sections 154, 155, and 156 into a single section governing property owner duties during riots and mob assemblies, increasing the maximum fine to ₹5,000.

title: Affray
old_text: IPC Section 159 defined affray (two or more persons fighting in a public place and disturbing public peace); Section 160 punished it with imprisonment up to 1 month or fine up to ₹100, or both.
new_text: Sub-section (1) defines affray (when two or more persons, by fighting in a public place, disturb the public peace); Sub-section (2) punishes affray with imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to one month, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 1 month, or fine up to ₹100, or both (IPC Section 160).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to one month, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both (BNS Section 194(2)).
explanation: Merges definition (IPC 159) and punishment (IPC 160) into one cohesive section while multiplying the maximum fine limit tenfold from ₹100 to ₹1,000.

title: Assaulting or obstructing public servant when suppressing riot, etc.
old_text: Penalized assaulting or obstructing a public servant endeavoring to disperse an unlawful assembly or suppress a riot with imprisonment up to 3 years or fine or both.
new_text: Whoever assaults or threatens to assault, or obstructs or attempts to obstruct, any public servant in the discharge of his duty of dispersing an unlawful assembly, or suppressing a riot or affray, shall be punished with imprisonment up to three years, or with fine, or with both.
punishment_old: Imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both (IPC Section 152).
punishment_new: Imprisonment of either description up to three years, or with fine, or with both (BNS Section 195).
explanation: Protects law enforcement personnel engaged in dispersing violent mobs, suppressing riots, or quelling public affrays. Renumbered from IPC Section 152.

title: Promoting enmity between different groups on grounds of religion, race, place of birth, residence, language, etc., and doing acts prejudicial to maintenance of harmony
old_text: Penalized promoting enmity between groups on religious, racial, linguistic, or caste grounds with imprisonment up to 3 years or fine; in places of worship up to 5 years and fine.
new_text: Sub-section (1): Whoever by words, signs, visible representations, or electronic communication promotes disharmony or feelings of enmity, hatred or ill-will between different religious, racial, or linguistic groups, shall be punished with imprisonment up to three years, or fine, or both. Sub-section (2): Offence committed in a place of worship or religious assembly carries imprisonment up to five years and fine.
punishment_old: General: up to 3 years or fine or both; Place of worship: up to 5 years and fine (IPC Section 153A).
punishment_new: General (196(1)): imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both; Place of worship (196(2)): imprisonment up to 5 years, and fine.
explanation: Key statutory provision penalizing hate speech and communal incitement, updated to explicitly encompass digital and electronic communications. Renumbered from IPC Section 153A.

title: Imputations, assertions prejudicial to national integration
old_text: Penalized imputations or assertions that any class cannot bear true allegiance to India or should be denied citizenship rights with imprisonment up to 3 years or fine; in places of worship up to 5 years.
new_text: Sub-section (1): Whoever by words, signs, visible representations, or electronic communication makes assertions prejudicial to national integration (such as asserting any group cannot bear true allegiance to India), shall be punished with imprisonment up to three years, or fine, or both. Sub-section (2): Offence committed in place of worship carries imprisonment up to five years and fine.
punishment_old: General: up to 3 years or fine or both; Place of worship: up to 5 years and fine (IPC Section 153B).
punishment_new: General (197(1)): imprisonment up to 3 years, or fine, or both; Place of worship (197(2)): imprisonment up to 5 years, and fine.
explanation: Penalizes questioning the patriotic loyalty or constitutional rights of any class of citizens, incorporating electronic mediums. Renumbered from IPC Section 153B.
